# Focus-wheel replacement brief

## Business context and supplied data
Willowbank runs three evening public sessions weekly. The fixture represents a manually turned wheel removed from a fictional telescope. The supplied dimensions are invented caliper-like inputs for an integration test, not measurements of any commercial telescope.

## Geometry and use
- Envelope: 38.0 mm maximum diameter and 18.0 mm overall height, including a 2 mm raised front hub.
- Six equally spaced shallow scallops; minimum grip diameter 33 mm. Round exposed edges with a nominal 1.0 mm radius.
- D shaft: 6.00 mm diameter; across-flat distance 5.20 mm. Blind socket depth 10.0 mm, concentric to the wheel. Add 0.20 mm radial clearance to the round boundary and 0.20 mm clearance to the flat. These are prototype choices, not verified fits.
- Retain at least 3.0 mm material above the blind socket. No set screw, metal insert, taper, or invented keyway.
- Target hand torque 0.15 N m and ambient use 0 to 35 degrees C; these are intended use assumptions, not validated performance requirements.

## Capabilities and internal policy
A P1S with 0.4 mm nozzle is the target machine. Desired production-prototype material is PETG, 0.20 mm layer height, four perimeters, and 35% infill; the installed matching machine/process/filament profiles must be selected explicitly. A PLA-only local environment may create a clearly named geometry prototype but must not label it PETG. Do not silently substitute profile material.

This part is for an unloaded training mechanism. Do not claim strength, fit, dimensional accuracy, standards compliance, or successful printing merely because files exist. Proposed dimension tolerance is +/-0.25 mm on non-mating surfaces. Record the D-socket design values separately from any later measured artifact values.

## Review and outputs
Review the socket interpretation, orientation, supports if needed, and exact final package. The dataset authorizes local generation and a labeled simulator receipt only. Real printer credentials, transfer, and print start are outside the pack. No special technical standard is asserted. Current tests inspect output-file existence; engineering validation remains pending.

steps.prompt:
Prepare a complete proposed digital geometry design for the next declared review, separating supplied requirements from your proposed construction choices. Preserve the 38 mm maximum diameter, 18 mm overall height including 2 mm front hub, six equally spaced shallow scallops, >=33 mm minimum grip, nominal 1 mm exposed rounds and subtle grip dots. The D socket uses the 6.00 mm round boundary and 5.20 mm across-flat shaft with 0.20 mm radial and flat clearance, 10 mm blind depth and >=3 mm material above it. No insert, set screw, taper or keyway. Preserve PETG/P1S 0.4/0.20 mm/four walls/35% profiles, proposed +/-0.25 mm non-mating tolerance and original human-review requirements. Propose explicit numeric scallop profile/depth/phase, hub diameter, dot count/dimensions/placement and exposed-edge treatment within the original limits; derive and record the D-boundary/flat construction and depth direction. These are design proposals, not additional requirements or verified fit. Distinguish decisions that must be resolved at this declared basis review from later inspection of actual geometry, supports and final package. Do not leave a predictable construction choice to a later unattended question. No geometry, fit, strength, standards or print-success claim yet. Do not ask runtime questions; output one complete proposal for the declared review. Keep the entire response below 3000 characters. Return only one valid JSON object, with no markdown, comments or trailing commas. Use these keys: supplied_requirements (short object), proposed_geometry (numeric dimensions plus short construction descriptions for scallops, hub, dots, rounds, socket and orientation), basis_review (short list of proposed choices requiring this review), remaining_verification (short list), engineering_acceptance (false). Expressions must be JSON strings; do not put equations in numeric values. Do not repeat input documents or provide lengthy rationale. This run supplies an explicit prior proposed geometry basis. Retain its numeric construction choices exactly instead of proposing replacements. It remains a proposal for this run's declared review, not engineering acceptance. Actual geometry and all original mandatory checks still follow.

# Focus-wheel replacement brief

## Business context and supplied data
Willowbank runs three evening public sessions weekly. The fixture represents a manually turned wheel removed from a fictional telescope. The supplied dimensions are invented caliper-like inputs for an integration test, not measurements of any commercial telescope.

## Geometry and use
- Envelope: 38.0 mm maximum diameter and 18.0 mm overall height, including a 2 mm raised front hub.
- Six equally spaced shallow scallops; minimum grip diameter 33 mm. Round exposed edges with a nominal 1.0 mm radius.
- D shaft: 6.00 mm diameter; across-flat distance 5.20 mm. Blind socket depth 10.0 mm, concentric to the wheel. Add 0.20 mm radial clearance to the round boundary and 0.20 mm clearance to the flat. These are prototype choices, not verified fits.
- Retain at least 3.0 mm material above the blind socket. No set screw, metal insert, taper, or invented keyway.
- Target hand torque 0.15 N m and ambient use 0 to 35 degrees C; these are intended use assumptions, not validated performance requirements.

## Capabilities and internal policy
A P1S with 0.4 mm nozzle is the target machine. Desired production-prototype material is PETG, 0.20 mm layer height, four perimeters, and 35% infill; the installed matching machine/process/filament profiles must be selected explicitly. A PLA-only local environment may create a clearly named geometry prototype but must not label it PETG. Do not silently substitute profile material.

This part is for an unloaded training mechanism. Do not claim strength, fit, dimensional accuracy, standards compliance, or successful printing merely because files exist. Proposed dimension tolerance is +/-0.25 mm on non-mating surfaces. Record the D-socket design values separately from any later measured artifact values.

## Review and outputs
Review the socket interpretation, orientation, supports if needed, and exact final package. The dataset authorizes local generation and a labeled simulator receipt only. Real printer credentials, transfer, and print start are outside the pack. No special technical standard is asserted. Current tests inspect output-file existence; engineering validation remains pending.

The outside diameter is 38 mm; use that as the image scale reference. The shaft is a 6.00 mm D shaft, with 5.20 mm from its flat to the far round surface. Make the blind socket 10 mm deep and allow the slip clearance in the notes. Please keep the raised grip dots subtle so gloves do not catch.

Produce the source mesh, repaired printable mesh, support/slicing preview, and P1S 0.4 mm PETG slice package. Keep the shaft opening facing up if it improves the bore. I need a local test transfer receipt after review; do not send anything to a physical printer.

# Focus-wheel replacement brief

## Business context and supplied data
Willowbank runs three evening public sessions weekly. The fixture represents a manually turned wheel removed from a fictional telescope. The supplied dimensions are invented caliper-like inputs for an integration test, not measurements of any commercial telescope.

## Geometry and use
- Envelope: 38.0 mm maximum diameter and 18.0 mm overall height, including a 2 mm raised front hub.
- Six equally spaced shallow scallops; minimum grip diameter 33 mm. Round exposed edges with a nominal 1.0 mm radius.
- D shaft: 6.00 mm diameter; across-flat distance 5.20 mm. Blind socket depth 10.0 mm, concentric to the wheel. Add 0.20 mm radial clearance to the round boundary and 0.20 mm clearance to the flat. These are prototype choices, not verified fits.
- Retain at least 3.0 mm material above the blind socket. No set screw, metal insert, taper, or invented keyway.
- Target hand torque 0.15 N m and ambient use 0 to 35 degrees C; these are intended use assumptions, not validated performance requirements.

## Capabilities and internal policy
A P1S with 0.4 mm nozzle is the target machine. Desired production-prototype material is PETG, 0.20 mm layer height, four perimeters, and 35% infill; the installed matching machine/process/filament profiles must be selected explicitly. A PLA-only local environment may create a clearly named geometry prototype but must not label it PETG. Do not silently substitute profile material.

This part is for an unloaded training mechanism. Do not claim strength, fit, dimensional accuracy, standards compliance, or successful printing merely because files exist. Proposed dimension tolerance is +/-0.25 mm on non-mating surfaces. Record the D-socket design values separately from any later measured artifact values.

## Review and outputs
Review the socket interpretation, orientation, supports if needed, and exact final package. The dataset authorizes local generation and a labeled simulator receipt only. Real printer credentials, transfer, and print start are outside the pack. No special technical standard is asserted. Current tests inspect output-file existence; engineering validation remains pending.

Produce the source mesh, repaired printable mesh, support/slicing preview, and P1S 0.4 mm PETG slice package. Keep the shaft opening facing up if it improves the bore. I need a local test transfer receipt after review; do not send anything to a physical printer.

- D shaft: 6.00 mm diameter; across-flat distance 5.20 mm. Blind socket depth 10.0 mm, concentric to the wheel. Add 0.20 mm radial clearance to the round boundary and 0.20 mm clearance to the flat. These are prototype choices, not verified fits.
- Retain at least 3.0 mm material above the blind socket. No set screw, metal insert, taper, or invented keyway.

# Focus-wheel replacement brief

## Business context and supplied data
Willowbank runs three evening public sessions weekly. The fixture represents a manually turned wheel removed from a fictional telescope. The supplied dimensions are invented caliper-like inputs for an integration test, not measurements of any commercial telescope.

## Geometry and use
- Envelope: 38.0 mm maximum diameter and 18.0 mm overall height, including a 2 mm raised front hub.
- Six equally spaced shallow scallops; minimum grip diameter 33 mm. Round exposed edges with a nominal 1.0 mm radius.
- D shaft: 6.00 mm diameter; across-flat distance 5.20 mm. Blind socket depth 10.0 mm, concentric to the wheel. Add 0.20 mm radial clearance to the round boundary and 0.20 mm clearance to the flat. These are prototype choices, not verified fits.
- Retain at least 3.0 mm material above the blind socket. No set screw, metal insert, taper, or invented keyway.
- Target hand torque 0.15 N m and ambient use 0 to 35 degrees C; these are intended use assumptions, not validated performance requirements.

## Capabilities and internal policy
A P1S with 0.4 mm nozzle is the target machine. Desired production-prototype material is PETG, 0.20 mm layer height, four perimeters, and 35% infill; the installed matching machine/process/filament profiles must be selected explicitly. A PLA-only local environment may create a clearly named geometry prototype but must not label it PETG. Do not silently substitute profile material.

This part is for an unloaded training mechanism. Do not claim strength, fit, dimensional accuracy, standards compliance, or successful printing merely because files exist. Proposed dimension tolerance is +/-0.25 mm on non-mating surfaces. Record the D-socket design values separately from any later measured artifact values.

## Review and outputs
Review the socket interpretation, orientation, supports if needed, and exact final package. The dataset authorizes local generation and a labeled simulator receipt only. Real printer credentials, transfer, and print start are outside the pack. No special technical standard is asserted. Current tests inspect output-file existence; engineering validation remains pending.

# Focus-wheel replacement brief

## Business context and supplied data
Willowbank runs three evening public sessions weekly. The fixture represents a manually turned wheel removed from a fictional telescope. The supplied dimensions are invented caliper-like inputs for an integration test, not measurements of any commercial telescope.

## Geometry and use
- Envelope: 38.0 mm maximum diameter and 18.0 mm overall height, including a 2 mm raised front hub.
- Six equally spaced shallow scallops; minimum grip diameter 33 mm. Round exposed edges with a nominal 1.0 mm radius.
- D shaft: 6.00 mm diameter; across-flat distance 5.20 mm. Blind socket depth 10.0 mm, concentric to the wheel. Add 0.20 mm radial clearance to the round boundary and 0.20 mm clearance to the flat. These are prototype choices, not verified fits.
- Retain at least 3.0 mm material above the blind socket. No set screw, metal insert, taper, or invented keyway.
- Target hand torque 0.15 N m and ambient use 0 to 35 degrees C; these are intended use assumptions, not validated performance requirements.

## Capabilities and internal policy
A P1S with 0.4 mm nozzle is the target machine. Desired production-prototype material is PETG, 0.20 mm layer height, four perimeters, and 35% infill; the installed matching machine/process/filament profiles must be selected explicitly. A PLA-only local environment may create a clearly named geometry prototype but must not label it PETG. Do not silently substitute profile material.

This part is for an unloaded training mechanism. Do not claim strength, fit, dimensional accuracy, standards compliance, or successful printing merely because files exist. Proposed dimension tolerance is +/-0.25 mm on non-mating surfaces. Record the D-socket design values separately from any later measured artifact values.

## Review and outputs
Review the socket interpretation, orientation, supports if needed, and exact final package. The dataset authorizes local generation and a labeled simulator receipt only. Real printer credentials, transfer, and print start are outside the pack. No special technical standard is asserted. Current tests inspect output-file existence; engineering validation remains pending.

# Focus-wheel replacement brief

## Business context and supplied data
Willowbank runs three evening public sessions weekly. The fixture represents a manually turned wheel removed from a fictional telescope. The supplied dimensions are invented caliper-like inputs for an integration test, not measurements of any commercial telescope.

## Geometry and use
- Envelope: 38.0 mm maximum diameter and 18.0 mm overall height, including a 2 mm raised front hub.
- Six equally spaced shallow scallops; minimum grip diameter 33 mm. Round exposed edges with a nominal 1.0 mm radius.
- D shaft: 6.00 mm diameter; across-flat distance 5.20 mm. Blind socket depth 10.0 mm, concentric to the wheel. Add 0.20 mm radial clearance to the round boundary and 0.20 mm clearance to the flat. These are prototype choices, not verified fits.
- Retain at least 3.0 mm material above the blind socket. No set screw, metal insert, taper, or invented keyway.
- Target hand torque 0.15 N m and ambient use 0 to 35 degrees C; these are intended use assumptions, not validated performance requirements.

## Capabilities and internal policy
A P1S with 0.4 mm nozzle is the target machine. Desired production-prototype material is PETG, 0.20 mm layer height, four perimeters, and 35% infill; the installed matching machine/process/filament profiles must be selected explicitly. A PLA-only local environment may create a clearly named geometry prototype but must not label it PETG. Do not silently substitute profile material.

This part is for an unloaded training mechanism. Do not claim strength, fit, dimensional accuracy, standards compliance, or successful printing merely because files exist. ## Review and outputs

# Focus-wheel replacement brief

## Business context and supplied data
Willowbank runs three evening public sessions weekly. The fixture represents a manually turned wheel removed from a fictional telescope. The supplied dimensions are invented caliper-like inputs for an integration test, not measurements of any commercial telescope.

## Geometry and use
- Envelope: 38.0 mm maximum diameter and 18.0 mm overall height, including a 2 mm raised front hub.
- Six equally spaced shallow scallops; minimum grip diameter 33 mm. Round exposed edges with a nominal 1.0 mm radius.
- D shaft: 6.00 mm diameter; across-flat distance 5.20 mm. Blind socket depth 10.0 mm, concentric to the wheel. Add 0.20 mm radial clearance to the round boundary and 0.20 mm clearance to the flat. These are prototype choices, not verified fits.
- Retain at least 3.0 mm material above the blind socket. No set screw, metal insert, taper, or invented keyway.
- Target hand torque 0.15 N m and ambient use 0 to 35 degrees C; these are intended use assumptions, not validated performance requirements.

## Capabilities and internal policy
A P1S with 0.4 mm nozzle is the target machine. Desired production-prototype material is PETG, 0.20 mm layer height, four perimeters, and 35% infill; the installed matching machine/process/filament profiles must be selected explicitly. A PLA-only local environment may create a clearly named geometry prototype but must not label it PETG. Do not silently substitute profile material.

This part is for an unloaded training mechanism. Do not claim strength, fit, dimensional accuracy, standards compliance, or successful printing merely because files exist. Proposed dimension tolerance is +/-0.25 mm on non-mating surfaces. Record the D-socket design values separately from any later measured artifact values.

## Review and outputs
Review the socket interpretation, orientation, supports if needed, and exact final package. The dataset authorizes local generation and a labeled simulator receipt only. Real printer credentials, transfer, and print start are outside the pack. No special technical standard is asserted. Current tests inspect output-file existence; engineering validation remains pending.
